item.title: Kerr named Scottish athlete of the year for third time in four years
item.description: Josh Kerr has been recognised for a record-breaking 2026 [Getty Images] Josh Kerr has been named Scotland's athlete of the year for the third time in four years after a record-breaking 2026. The 29-year-old was recognised for a standout year in which he shattered the mile world record and won gold at both the World Indoor Championships and Commonwealth Games. "It puts a cap on an awesome end to the year," Kerr said. "It's been a long hard year, but I'm excited about it and looking forward to next year. "The thing now with Scottish Athletics is you know you have to kind of be right at the top of what you're doing to be able to even be in contention for these awards. "There are no limits on what Scottish athletes can achieve. Any limits are just the ones you put on yourself. "If you can dream big enough, and you really believe and put the work in, then you're hopefully going to get as close as possible to it. "In some instances, you might get everything you want." Melanie Woods, who won double Commonwealth gold, was voted Para-athlete of the Year, with Sophie Thomas and Alistair Street named U20 Athlete of the Year and U18 Athlete of the Year respectively.

item.description: MILWAUKEE, WI - OCTOBER 23: Nick Martinez #28 of the Tampa Bay Rays reacts at the end of the fifth inning during Game One of the 2026 World Series presented by Capital One between the Tampa Bay Rays and the Milwaukee Brewers at American Family Field on Friday, October 23, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by Daniel Shirey/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images The San Diego Padres are desperate for starting pitching and everyone knows it. That is why the club is rumored to be in on pitchers at every level of the market, including the top pitching free agent Tarik Skubal. Earlier this week it was also reported the Padres are in on the Japanese arms looking to transition to MLB as well as established veterans like Dustin May , Freddy Peralta, Nick Martinez and Matthew Boyd . San Diego is also reportedly interested in bringing back Michael King and Nick Pivetta. With only a couple of weeks before the expiration of the CBA and the expected lockout on Dec. 1, the pitching additions could come fast and furious. Like most seasons, the first domino to fall is usually the top free agent. In this offseason that is Skubal. The left-hander is expected to have meeting with several clubs starting next week and one of those clubs is the Padres. Whether or not they have a legitimate chance to add the star pitcher is anyone’s guess, but if new owners Jose E. Feliciano and Kwanza Jones wanted to make a statement about their commitment to building a winning roster that would be one way to do it. With so many needs in the San Diego rotation, the question has been whether or not committing a large sum of payroll to one arm like Skubal would be wise. For the same money the Padres might be able to bring back King and then add two or three additional starters like May, Martinez or Peralta. Of course there are also the Japanese pitchers to consider and what those monetary commitments would look like. With all the talk about pitching this offseason, San Diego’s pursuit of another bat and the need to address first base has taken a back seat. Ty France remains unsigned but he just saw Jake Bauers parlay his season in Milwaukee into a lucrative contract with the Boston Red Sox. Perhaps that deal gives a framework for a France deal whether that is with the Padres or any other team. General manager A.J. Preller has a stated he has a budget, what that is no one outside of the top brass in San Diego knows. The potential moves over the next two weeks could be very telling in that regard, but for now all anyone can do is wait and speculate. item.title: Stewart Cink on verge of Charles Schwab Cup with 18 holes to go at Phoenix Country Club
item.description: They came into the week 1-2. They'll start the final round of the Charles Schwab Cup Championship 1-2. OK, technically 1-T2, as Stewart Cink holds the 54-hole lead at Phoenix Country Club while Zach Johnson is tied for second with 18 to go. The season-ending event on the PGA Tour Champions also determines the winner of the season-long points race and only Cink and Johnson can win it. Cink leads the tournament at 17 under after a third-round 68. Johnson is tied with Scott Hend at 14 under after Johnson shot 64 on Saturday. Hend blistered the course for a 62 to vault into contention. It's the best score of the week at Phoenix Country Club, thanks to five straight birdies on Nos. 4 through 8. Cink, 53, is seeking his 10 Champions win and his second straight in Phoenix. Should he win the tournament, he'll also win the Cup and claim both trophies for a second year in a row. Only three golfers have won the Schwab double and he'd be the first to do it twice (as well as the first to do it in two straight years). He would also be the eighth player to win the season title more than once: Bernhard Langer (6), Steven Alker (2), Tom Lehman (2), Loren Roberts (2), Jay Haas (2), Tom Watson (2), Hale Irwin (2). "It would mean a whole lot," he said of repeating as the champion of both trophies. "It's been a goal of mine since the start of 2025, and I've been talking about it and putting it out there and sort of putting the pressure on myself in a way. I know what it feels like to win, so I just have so much respect for all these players that to finish on top is something I would be really proud of. It's just such a great collection of golfers and they've got so much experience. item.title: WPL 2027: BCCI shifts Mumbai leg from Brabourne to Wankhede on ICC request; here's why
item.description: The Mumbai leg of the Women’s Premier League (WPL) 2027 will be held at the Wankhede Stadium instead of the Brabourne Stadium, the BCCI announced on Sunday. The dates and fixtures of the tournament will remain unchanged. The fifth edition of the WPL will be played from January 14 to February 7, with Vadodara and Mumbai serving as the two host cities. The first leg will take place at the BCA Stadium in Vadodara from January 14 to 24, while Mumbai will host the remaining matches from January 26 until the final on February 7. The Mumbai leg was originally scheduled to be held at the Cricket Club of India’s (CCI) Brabourne Stadium. However, the venue has been changed as CCI is also set to host the inaugural edition of the ICC Women's Champions Trophy in the T20 format, which begins on February 14. The BCCI said the gap between the two tournaments would not give the pitches enough time to recover. “The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) has announced that the Mumbai leg of the Women’s Premier League 2027 will now be held at Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai, instead of the Brabourne Stadium at the Cricket Club of India (CCI). The dates and fixtures will remain unchanged,” the BCCI said in a statement. “The WPL Governing Council approved the original venues and dates for the fifth edition of the TATA WPL at its meeting on 15 September 2026. Under the approved schedule, the Mumbai leg, comprising Match Nos. 12 to 20, the Eliminator and the Final, was to be played at CCI between 26 January and 7 February 2027.” “As CCI is also scheduled to host the inaugural ICC Women’s Champions Trophy 2027, commencing on 14 February, the interval between the conclusion of the TATA WPL and the start of the multi-nation tournament would not provide sufficient time for the pitches to recover,” the board added. The BCCI said the venue was changed following a request from the International Cricket Council (ICC). The WPL Committee has approved the change, with Wankhede Stadium set to host all 11 matches of the Mumbai leg. “The change follows a request from the International Cricket Council (ICC) to shift the matches scheduled to be played at CCI. The WPL Committee has approved the change, with Wankhede Stadium now set to host all 11 matches of the Mumbai leg,” the BCCI said. The Mumbai Cricket Association (MCA), during its 95th Annual General Meeting, had formally requested the BCCI to consider it for hosting matches in case of changes to the schedules of future series.

item.title: Barcelona midfielder eyeing return vs Deportivo after speedy recovery
item.description: Barcelona midfielder eyeing return vs Deportivo after speedy recovery Barcelona were dealt a massive blow earlier this month when star midfielder Rodri picked up a thigh injury and was subsequently ruled out for at least four weeks. The midfielder has since been working on his fitness and has made a relatively speedy recovery, as he looks to get back onto the pitch as soon as possible. A recent report from Diario AS has offered an update on Rodri’s fitness, suggesting that his return could come sooner than expected. Speedy recovery for Rodri Barcelona have missed the presence of Rodri in midfield. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) The report points out that Rodri’s expected return timeline has been moved earlier following the midfielder’s rapid progress during recovery. Although Barcelona never gave an injury timeline for Rodri, it was expected that the injury would take around four to five weeks to recover. The Barcelona new signing was expected to return to action during the second week of December, perhaps for the Champions League game against his former club Manchester City. However, thanks to Rodri’s hard work during recovery, he is expected to return to action much sooner than that. When will Rodri return? Rodri is hopeful of returning vs Atletico Madrid. (Photo by Pedro Salado/Getty Images) The report adds that Rodri could receive the medical discharge from the Barcelona board as soon as the end of November. The idea is for the veteran midfielder to appear against Deportivo on November 29 by making a late appearance and get his eye in. Rodri will then try to make it into the starting eleven against Atletico Madrid on December 2. He is more than likely to be available for the matches against Celta Vigo and Manchester City, which was a doubt not too long ago. That means the Spanish international will only miss Barcelona’s next two games against Villarreal and Sabah, in what appears to be a massive boost for coach Hansi Flick. The Catalans have also received a favourable report on Dani Olmo, who is expected to return against Villarreal , having almost completed his recovery process.

item.title: Back from the dead? Dana White open to Kayla Harrison-Amanda Nunes rematch at 145 — ‘I’d do it again’
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 14: (L-R) Kayla Harrison reacts after her submission victory over Amanda Nunes of Brazil in their women's bantamweight championship fight during the UFC 334 event at Madison Square Garden on November 14, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC) Double or nothing? Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) Bantamweight queen Kayla Harrison decisively defeated former two-division champion Amanda Nunes in UFC 334 ’s co-main event last night (Sat., Nov. 14, 2026), submitting the returning “Lioness” with a rear-naked choke in the fourth round inside Madison Square Garden in New York City ( watch highlights ). But that doesn’t mean their business is completely finished. During the UFC 334 post-fight press conference ( watch here ), UFC CEO Dana White was asked if he would consider booking an immediate rematch between Harrison and Nunes at 145 pounds. “Sure, yeah,” White said. “I’d do it again.” Harrison proposed that exact scenario before UFC 334, promising Nunes an automatic rematch at Featherweight if she successfully defended her Bantamweight championship. “I feel like I am going to prove I’m the champion on Saturday night,” Harrison said during the pre-fight press conference. “And then I’ll give her an automatic rematch at 145 so I can snatch that other belt.” There is just one slight problem: that “other belt” technically doesn’t exist anymore. Nunes retired in June 2023 while holding UFC’s Bantamweight and Featherweight titles. The promotion never crowned a new 145-pound champion, developed official rankings or attempted to rebuild the division, effectively shutting it down after “Lioness” walked away. White’s response confirmed he would consider staging the rematch at 145 pounds, but he did not say whether UFC would officially resurrect the Featherweight championship for it … please no. Moving back up would certainly appeal to Harrison, who previously competed at Lightweight and Featherweight before making the brutal cut to 135 pounds for her UFC run. After defeating Nunes, the 36-year-old admitted she remains uncertain about her fighting future. “I have a lot of decisions to make when I get home,” Harrison said. “Every time I cut weight, I say never again. So we’ll see. I definitely have some injuries after that fight that I’ll need to heal up.” Harrison has teased retirement several times and said before UFC 334 that she could walk away from combat sports satisfied with everything she has accomplished. Nunes’ future is equally uncertain. The 38-year-old returned from more than three years in retirement specifically to challenge Harrison, but did not give a post-fight interview or announce whether she intends to compete again following her submission loss. So, while White is open to running it back at 145 pounds, there is also a legitimate possibility that Harrison, Nunes—or both—never fight again. item.title: Rory McIlroy talks after winning his eighth Race to Dubai title: ‘I’m very proud of myself right now’
item.description: Photo by Warren Little/Getty Images Rory McIlroy has outlined how proud he is to have won an eighth Race to Dubai title following a dramatic battle with Eugenio Chacarra on Sunday at the DP World Tour Championship. It was Tyrrell Hatton who comfortably won the final event of the season. However, all eyes were on the battle between McIlroy and Chacarra, with the pair vying for the Order of Merit crown on the DP World Tour. The Northern Irishman definitely did not have his A game for much of the day, particularly on the greens. However, he was able to put himself on pole position to win the Race to Dubai as he looked set to finish second on the Earth Course. And when the chasing pack failed to catch him, it was confirmed that McIlroy had edged out Chacarra and won the season-long race. Rory McIlroy reflects on catching Colin Montgomerie with his latest Race to Dubai win Of course, McIlroy’s triumph moves himself alongside Colin Montgomerie for the most Order of Merit victories. And speaking after the final round in Dubai, McIlroy explained how proud he was to make further history in his career. “I don’t really know what to say. Winning eight Order of Merits was never really in my list of goals when I was growing up. I remember Monty being obviously a stalwart of the European Tour, going to watch him at the World Match Play at Wentworth over the years. I remember playing with him for the first time at The London Club at The European Open in 2008,” he said. “So to pull up alongside him and to win eight of these things, yeah, it means the world to me. I’m a very proud European. I’m a proud European player. I’m proud to be a part of the DP World Tour. item.description: Rico Lewis Reveals the Most Important Lesson He Learned From Pep Guardiola at Manchester City Rico Lewis broke into the Manchester City first-team squad under Pep Guardiola in 2022. Ask what a young player picks up under Pep Guardiola and the obvious answers are tactical: positional rotations, inverted full-backs and the endless drills that turned Manchester City into a passing machine. Lewis, one of the few City Football Academy graduates, to successfully become a first-team regular during the Catalan’s decade at the club, has a different answer. Alongside Phil Foden and Nico O’Reilly, Lewis holds the rare distinction of going from an U18s star to someone Guardiola trusted in big games and with regular starts. When asked recently what he learned from four years under the legendary coach, the 21-year-old says the lesson that truly stuck had nothing to do with shape or system. The power of collective belief Speaking to Give Me Sport , Lewis was asked what he had taken from Guardiola and how he was adjusting to life under a new manager. “Obviously Pep was very demanding and rightfully so. I think that’s the way you win things,” the full-back said. Lewis broke into the City first-team in a year of relentless winning; within 10 months of his Premier League debut (against Bournemouth in August 2022), the Blues had won a historic treble. Other career highlights include scoring in an FA Cup semi-final and earning his first caps for England’s senior squad, although he recently went nearly two years without being called up by Thomas Tuchel. He pointed to the mentality of the squad at the time as the biggest reason why Manchester City were the dominant force in English football for nearly all of Guardiola’s tenure. “The togetherness of the team and the belief in the system and the belief that we’re going to win - I think that’s greater than any tactic, going into every game thinking we’re going to win this game, we’re better than the other team," Lewis added. Guardiola has since moved on, with Enzo Maresca now steering Manchester City through a packed schedule, and Lewis has had to adjust to new methods and fresh ideas in the process. The England international said: “You can take that [belief] with you wherever you go, instead of a tactic or a system. item.title: Clippers rookie Keaton Wagler draws praise from Shai Gilgeous-Alexander
item.description: Keaton Wagler continues to find his footing in his first season with the Los Angeles Clippers . The fifth overall pick in the 2026 draft has found a way to contribute to coach Tyronn Lue’s team, averaging 12.4 points, 3.4 rebounds and 3.2 assists through 11 games played this season. The rookie has not made his first official start but has averaged 22.7 minutes per game off the bench. Wagler modeled part of his game after Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, who spent his rookie season with the Clippers in 2018 before he was later traded to the Oklahoma City Thunder . Being in the NBA has afforded Wagler opportunities early in the season to play against some of his idols with the Clippers having played the Thunder twice this season. "It was a cool experience," Wagler told reporters about being able to play against Gilgeous-Alexander. "Growing up I really liked Shai, his game and being able to go up against him." Wagler has drawn praise from Gilgeous-Alexander after those two meetings. "He has good feel. Can really shoot," Gilgeous-Alexander said about the rookie after the Clippers' 113-112 victory against the Thunder on Friday, Nov. 13. "Usually when you have those things, the game will slow down for you eventually. "He’s in a good situation where he can play a lot. There are good coaches over there, so he’ll learn the game the right way. As long as he works hard, he should have a long runway to be whoever he wants to be." Tyronn Lue issues apology to Keaton Wagler The Clippers have struggled to start the season, winning just three of their first 11 games, including Friday's victory against the Thunder. Earlier this month, Lue apologized to the rookie for not getting him more playing time. "That's just what I felt like," Lue said about Wagler’s minutes after a 117-116 overtime loss to the Miami Heat on Nov. 4. Wagler played a season-low 16 minutes against Miami. He finished with 11 points and a team-high +15 while on the court. Lue told reporters on Nov. 8 that he had apologized to Wagler after having rewatched the film from the game, telling him he earned more playing time than he received. Wagler averaged 19.6 minutes per game over the last three games since Lue's apology. item.description: Saturday marked the first time Wales had beaten New Zealand in 73 years [Getty Images] Welsh rugby fans were "fizzing off their heads" on Saturday night after ending 73 years of hurt against New Zealand in an epic Nations Championship encounter. The match at the Principality Stadium ended 35-28 to the hosts as the All Blacks' run of 34 successive victories against Wales - dating back to 1953 - came to a juddering halt in Cardiff. Wales fans were left stunned by a result that came just a week on from having to grind out a win against Japan. Prince William, patron of the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) also congratulated the team on the win, saying it was a "fantastic result". But the approach backfired spectacularly after a brilliant performance sparked astonishing scenes in Cardiff . A crowd of 55,152 could scarcely believe what had unfolded, and there were scenes of wild celebration with players in tears as Wales began taking in arguably the most famous win of their 145-year Test match history. item.description: John Jones-Imagn Images On Saturday night in Harrison, New Jersey, an international friendly pitting Club America against the New York Red Bulls escalated into a violent street fight. The match ended with a 1-0 win for the Red Bulls, but the final score was forgotten after a massive brawl broke out in the 85th minute. Five players received red cards, and fans threw objects onto the field during the chaos. The trouble started after a foul near the end line caused a confrontation that quickly escalated into a free-for-all. Players from both sides threw punches and kicked each other while referees tried to separate the group. Footage revealed Red Bulls midfielder Andy Rojas seemingly striking Club America’s Dagoberto Espinoza on the back of the head. Violence on the Pitch The brawl involved players from both clubs wrestling and fighting as officials scrambled to restore order. New York’s Ronald Donkor and Nehuen Benedetti received dismissals for their involvement in the brawl. Club America also lost three players, including Emilio Lara, Ramón Juarez, and Espinoza, who was the target of the punch from Rojas. It remains unclear if Rojas will face additional punishment from league officials for his actions. Fans made the situation worse by launching projectiles onto the pitch, adding a dangerous element to an already volatile scene. The New York Post reported that the atmosphere turned from a spirited exhibition into an international incident. The Red Bulls walked away with the victory, but the ugly brawl defined the night more than the game itself. Club America must now regroup before facing Tigres on Nov. 25 for the Liga MX Apertura finale. Coaches React to the Chaos Following the match, Red Bulls coach Michael Bradley appeared unconcerned regarding the on-field fireworks. He explained that players always want to compete and win, even in games that are supposed to be just for fun. Bradley told reporters, “You hear people say that there are no real friendlies,” noting that the desire to win never goes away. He added, “It’s part of it on certain nights.” The coach’s comments suggest that while the violence was extreme, the competitive nature of the players was the main driver. A tuneup during the international window transformed a standard soccer match into a full-blown fight.
